title: fix(update): clear model retirement warnings after repair completes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A completed update repair can still report “Model retirement deferred until configured plugin installation converges.” The same stale warning can survive in final results, indexed update warnings, and later Doctor history.

## User Impact

The warning clears when the selected update run has durably completed model retirement. Unfinished, failed, missing, or unreadable completion evidence keeps the warning. Unrelated advisories and execution failures retain their meaning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retirement owner already records completion, but the shared warning reconciliation only recognized plugin-specific migration warnings. This change uses that existing same-run receipt across finalization, convergence, Doctor publication, and selected historical reports. Historical records remain intact.

Incoming structured steps and their indexed warning rows are reconciled together. An explicitly empty current warning list is authoritative, while advisory kind, nonzero advisory exit classification, raw output, and failure facts remain available. The existing shared helper replaces the plugin-only helper; there is no new storage, schema, configuration, or timeout policy.

## Evidence

- Red-first [CI 40811694869](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40811694869) reproduces the historical warning on Node and Bun and reaches the intended real-repair warning assertions on Bun. The full repair regression now uses the established registered-CLI route, exercising real Doctor/config persistence under normal command budgets.
- [Native Testbox proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40821304985) passed 49 selected tests on Node and 49 on pinned Bun at source `9f172cf0e96a99f8b20048cb122cdcdece7eb0bf` and its qualified dependency inputs. Each runtime intentionally excludes 37 unrelated lifecycle cases. Production remains unchanged in the final fixture correction. The worker had 4 CPUs and 16 GB RAM.
- The original native wrapper exited 1 during final cleanup verification after all selected tests passed. One supported stop of that same allocation succeeded, and native inspection confirmed completed remote settlement. This reconciled cleanup outcome is recorded separately; the original failure is not relabeled as a successful wrapper run. Hosted PR CI remains a separate landing gate.
- Fresh [fixture correction proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40824959942) at final source `548014f0084d6fb8c00a23e69a93d1e66711fdc4` passes targeted lint (0 warnings/errors) and all three affected convergence cases on both Node and pinned Bun. The complete step now goes directly through the existing advisory producer, resolving the CI map-spread error without changing production or assertions. This native wrapper exited 0 with settled cleanup; these six executions are separate from the prior 98-test run.
- Coverage includes same-run completed/skipped/failed/missing evidence, foreign active completion, unreadable history, unrelated advisories, real final repair output, Doctor publication, all three convergence paths, and preexisting indexed warning rows.
- Production delta: +92 lines, required to keep current structured warnings and persisted warning indices consistent without losing execution classification. Regression test delta: +244 lines, allocated exactly for these owner-boundary and real-flow cases. No shared scalar ratchet edit.
